title: Fonts & Typography
definition: CSS properties used to control the appearance of text, including the font family, weight, size, and spacing.
simpleExplanation: By default, browsers use boring fonts like Times New Roman. Typography properties allow you to load beautiful custom fonts from Google Fonts, make them bold, italicized, spaced out, or transformed to ALL CAPS.
realWorldExample: Loading the 'Inter' or 'Roboto' font from Google Fonts to give a web app a sleek, modern, Apple-like aesthetic.

intermediate: Why do we write fallback fonts like `font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;`?

answers.question: Why fallback fonts?
answers.answer: If the user's computer doesn't have 'Arial' installed, the browser moves to the next option and tries 'Helvetica'. If they don't have that either, it falls back to the generic system 'sans-serif' font. It ensures the site doesn't break.
